newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian protesters angered by savings loss.
newsitem.headline: Albanian protesters angered by savings loss.

text.p: The manager of an Albanian pyramid scheme told thousands of angry demonstrators on Wednesday their savings scheme had collapsed, hours after they clashed with riot police in a protest to recover their money.

Maksude Kademi, a 30-year-old Romany gypsy woman, who in November stopped repayments to depositors in one of the most high profile get-rich-quick projects, told a jeering crowd she had no money to give them.
"This was a pyramid scheme that failed. So you have no reason to (protest and) ask the state to give you money," Kademi told the crowd of several thousand through a megaphone.

"I asked for a credit today but I could not get it. I will keep trying," she added, drawing boos and whistles from demonstrators, some of whom tried to break a police cordon barring them from her western Tirana flat.
Earlier about 500 depositors clashed with riot police near Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square. There were several arrests and some protesters were injured.
Pyramid schemes, offering returns of up to 200 percent over three months, have sprung up across the impoverished Balkan state since the fall of communism in 1990.
